episodes.170052: A moderately strong shortwave and surface cold front moved across a moderate to highly unstable airmass across VT during the early afternoon hours of July 21st. Scattered thunderstorms developed and quickly intensified, some producing damaging winds and hail with one supercell that moved across Orleans and Essex counties with several reports of large hail, up to golf ball size and some scattered tree damage.
episodes.170066: Several outflow boundary existed across the region on the afternoon of the 21st which initiated isolated thunderstorm development. Strong instability and DCAPE allowed one storm to produce a severe wind gust near Abernathy (Hale County). This storm went on to produce a 57 mph wind gust at Lubbock Preston Smith International Airport (Lubbock County).
episodes.170067: Moisture values continued to be on the rise across northern and central New Mexico on July 20, 2022, and this led to a very active monsoon day for the area. Scattered to numerous thunderstorms were common across much of the area, particularly across the mountainous terrain. New Mexico's recent burn scars continued to  be magnets for heavy thunderstorms with known impacts across the McBride burn scar as well as the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar. Meanwhile, thunderstorms also produced brief strong winds in a couple locations.
episodes.170069: While thunderstorm coverage was not as widespread compared to the previous day, July 21, 2022, was still a very active monsoon day for northern New Mexico in part due to the training of thunderstorms along the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar. Thunderstorms developed early in the day with steering flow tracking them slowly towards the southeast. Thunderstorms continuously developed along the Sangre de Cristo Mountains through the daytime hours, and thus, kept impacting the same areas. The Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar was hit particularly hard with rainfall estimated of at least two to four inches with locally higher amounts likely. Highway 518 near Holman and Cleveland, which had been hit hard the previous day, were hit hard again with significant flooding and debris flow observed. The southern portion of the burn scar also received significant rainfall totals, and unfortunately, this flooding took the lives of three individuals at Camp Blue Haven.
episodes.170080: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of eastern Oklahoma during the afternoon and evening of the 21st. The thunderstorms were high-based, and had a deep layer of dry air between the cloud bases and the ground, which resulted in an enhancement of the downdraft momentum due to evaporative cooling into the dry air. A similar environment was in place on the 22nd, with strong to severe thunderstorms once again developing in the afternoon and evening. The strongest storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.170081: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of northwestern Arkansas during the afternoon and evening of the 21st. The thunderstorms were high-based, and had a deep layer of dry air between the cloud bases and the ground, which resulted in an enhancement of the downdraft momentum due to evaporative cooling into the dry air. The strongest storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.170343: A surface cold front moved southeastward from southeastern Lower Michigan and far-northwest Ohio to central Lake Erie and north-central and southwestern portions of Ohio during the evening of the 20th. Bands of organized thunderstorms, mainly in the form of multicells, occurred along and especially ahead of the front. These storms encountered a warm sector comprised of moderate to strong effective bulk shear and MUCAPE, respectively, and strong DCAPE. This environment allowed sporadic convective straight-line wind damage to occur. A supercell embedded within the pre-frontal squall line generated a brief tornado in far-southern Wayne and far-northern Holmes Counties as the supercell encountered favorably-low mixed layer LCL's and large surface-based effective SRH.
episodes.170429: Isolated thunderstorms moved across far northeast Illinois during the late afternoon and early evening of July 21st.
episodes.170644: A pre-frontal trough of low pressure in western New England combined with instability and just enough shear to produce a broken line of severe thunderstorms in western MA and northern CT in the late afternoon.  A significant microburst occurred in Erving and Warwick, MA.
episodes.170646: A pre-frontal trough of low pressure in western New England combined with instability and just enough shear to produce a broken line of severe thunderstorms in western MA and northern CT in the mid afternoon. A significant microburst occurred in Erving and Warwick, MA.
episodes.170740: An isolated severe thunderstorm occurred. The thunderstorm occurred in a very moist and unstable southwest wind flow, well in advance of a cold front over the central Plains.
episodes.170771: A couple of thunderstorms produced sporadic instances of wind damage when a surface trough interacted with the bay breeze.
episodes.170772: A couple of thunderstorms produced sporadic instances of wind damage when a surface trough interacted with the bay breeze.
episodes.170773: A couple of thunderstorms produced sporadic instances of wind damage when a surface trough interacted with the bay breeze.
episodes.170781: Showers and thunderstorms developed during the evening hours along a cold front moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.170866: A couple of thunderstorms produced sporadic instances of gusty winds when a surface trough interacted with the bay breeze.
episodes.171056: A slow moving cold front was the main culprit behind showers and storms that prevailed across West Virginia between July 21st and 23rd. Strong to severe storms thrived during the afternoon hours, and often caused blown down trees and power lines from damaging wind gusts.
episodes.171106: A thunderstorm tracked across southern Delaware during the afternoon and produced isolated areas of wind damage.
episodes.171107: An isolated thunderstorm produced some minor wind damage near Marlton in southern New Jersey.
episodes.171124: Severe thunderstorms impacted southeast Arkansas on the evening of July 21st. One of these severe storms moved through Chicot County where large hail up to quarter size was observed.
episodes.171185: A series of cold fronts and disturbances passed through southeast Ohio from July 20th to 23rd, with daily afternoon showers and thunderstorms ensuing. Storms that occurred from the 20th to 22nd resulted in some minor tree damage, but the more substantial activity arrived on the 23rd, when trees and power lines were knocked down.
episodes.171324: A warm front crossed the region during the morning of the 21st. A cold front and strong upper level disturbance then crossed the region during the afternoon and evening. Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and persisted into the evening. Isolated severe thunderstorms produced large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.171967: Two cold fronts swept across Arkansas bringing several rounds of severe thunderstorms to the region.
episodes.172039: A cold front sweeping through the area combined with a warm and unstable airmass spawned a few thunderstorms. One of these storms produced damaging winds in Caswell county.
episodes.172048: Isolated severe storms resulted in several reports of damaging wind gusts which resulted in several downed trees and tree limbs and power outages.
episodes.172058: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms pushed southeast across portions of northern Alabama during the early morning hours. One storm knocked down a tree southeast of Barton in Colbert County.
episodes.172120: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of an eastward progressing cold front on July 21, 2022. A few became severe producing damaging wind gusts and hail. Most of the severe weather occurred along and just east of the Hudson Valley.
episodes.172121: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of an eastward progressing cold front on July 21, 2022. A few became severe producing damaging wind gusts and hail. Heavy rain led to some street flooding in downtown Bennington.
episodes.172122: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of an eastward progressing cold front on July 21, 2022. A few became severe producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.172148: A line of thunderstorms with scattered instances of damaging wind gusts crossed eastern Ohio during the evening hours of July 20th. Due to the later timing and the resultant loss of instability, the storms diminished in intensity as they approached the Ohio River.
episodes.172209: An upper level short wave trough moving through the region resulted in severe thunderstorms developing over south central North Dakota. Initially, a severe thunderstorm quickly developed and moved through the Bismarck and Lincoln areas of Burleigh County, with a second storm developing right behind the first one following a similar track. There was a report of tennis ball size hail in the north side of Bismarck, with most locations seeing quarter to golf ball size hail. The area around the Bismarck Airport received no hail. Where hail fell there was widespread roof and vehicle damage. Additional severe storms developed to the south and east, resulting in many reports of crop damage. Although hail was the main threat with these storms, one storm produced reported 65 mph wind gusts near Zeeland in McIntosh County.
episodes.172236: A MCS over Tennessee during the morning hours of July 21 pushed an outflow boundary into north Alabama in the afternoon. The air mass was very unstable south of the outflow boundary with surface based CAPE 3500-4500 J/kg and DCAPE 1300-1500 J/kg.  The storms that initiated in the afternoon organized into QLCS that produced widespread damaging winds, large hail, and flash flooding.
episodes.172286: A cold front and weak upper level trough crossed the mountains and moved into central Virginia during the afternoon on July 21. This resulted in the development of scattered severe thunderstorms which produced gusty winds.
episodes.172287: A weak upper level trough moved into Maryland during the afternoon on July 21. This resulted in the development of scattered severe thunderstorms which produced gusty winds.
episodes.172311: Scattered thunderstorms, which produced gusty winds, developed off of a weak upper level trough and moved over the Rappahannock River during the afternoon on July 21.
episodes.172312: A cold front stalled near the Ohio Valley on the evening of July 20th. Unusually high instability ahead of the front fueled thunderstorm development late in the evening over southcentral Kentucky just ahead of the front. Moderate shear helped organize the storms as they shifted eastward and evolved into a line of quick-moving storms. The strongest winds occurred from Breathitt County southeastward to the Virginia/Kentucky border during the early morning hours of July 21st. Storm backbuilding and training occurred along the southern edge of the line, leading to substantial rainfall along the Virginia border.
episodes.172314: Scattered thunderstorms, which produced gusty winds, developed off of a weak upper level trough and moved over the James River during the late afternoon on July 21.
episodes.172315: Scattered thunderstorms, which produced gusty winds, developed off of a weak upper level trough and moved over the Chesapeake Bay during the late afternoon on July 21.
episodes.172316: Scattered thunderstorms, which produced gusty winds, developed off of a weak upper level trough and moved over the Virginia Coastal Waters during the late afternoon on July 21.
episodes.172341: Several waves of thunderstorms developed over southern Ontario ahead of an approaching weak cold front. While the initial waves of convection fizzled out as they approached the Niagara Peninsula, the final wave held together and crossed into the Niagara Frontier interacting with increasing shear and instability resulting in several reports of thunderstorm wind damage into the early morning hours.
episodes.172342: Several waves of thunderstorms developed over southern Ontario ahead of an approaching weak cold front. While the initial waves of convection fizzled out as they approached the Niagara Peninsula, the final wave held together and crossed into the Niagara Frontier interacting with increasing shear and instability resulting in several reports of thunderstorm wind damage into the early morning hours.
episodes.172343: Several waves of thunderstorms developed over southern Ontario ahead of an approaching weak cold front. While the initial waves of convection fizzled out as they approached the Niagara Peninsula, the final wave held together and crossed into the Niagara Frontier interacting with increasing shear and instability resulting in several reports of thunderstorm wind damage into the early morning hours.
episodes.172367: During the evening and overnight hours of July 20th into July 21st, strong to severe thunderstorms developed out ahead of an approaching cold front. On the afternoon of July 20th, temperatures surged into the mid-90s across central Kentucky, with dewpoint temperatures reaching the mid-70s. The warm and unstable low levels, combined with mid-level height falls from an approaching trough, allowed for greater than 4000 J/kg mixed-layer CAPE across portions of south central Kentucky during the evening hours of July 20th. Despite some boundary layer stabilization during the late evening hours, a low-level jet allowed for convection to sustain itself through the overnight hours, with scattered wind damage being observed mainly across south central Kentucky. While convection was initially fairly discrete in nature, after midnight, an evolution toward one large convective complex was observed, which contributed to additional flash flooding issues across south central Kentucky.
episodes.172430: A line of thunderstorms moved eastward through central North Carolina during the early afternoon hours, within an increasingly warm, moist environment ahead of a surface trough and southward moving cold front. Several of the storms produced damaging wind gusts as they moved through the Triad toward the Triangle of central North Carolina in the evening hours.
episodes.172432: A pre-frontal trough was present across western North Carolina amid a warm and moist airmass. A cold front moved southeast into the northern Mid-Atlantic, Ohio Valley, and the mid-south toward the morning of the 21st. Ahead of these surface boundaries, scattered showers and storms developed over southern North Carolina in the evening, from the southern Piedmont, eastward across the Sandhills and southern Coastal Plain. Some of the storms over Stanly and Moore Counties produced tree and power line damage.
episodes.172499: A shortwave trough shifted southeast across the region along the eastern periphery of an upper-level ridge centered over the Desert Southwest. At the surface, a weak cold front extended from the southern Texas Panhandle eastward into southeast Oklahoma and southwest Arkansas. These features combined to produce isolated severe thunderstorms across Howard County in southwest Arkansas during peak diurnal heating, as instability spiked along and ahead of the surface boundary while deep layer shear also increased. Due to the extreme heat south of the boundary, high cloud bases presented a threat of downburst winds with some of the strongest thunderstorms, which eventually produced isolated damaging wind gusts in parts of Howard County during the late afternoon hours.
episodes.172503: Monsoon moisture surged back across northern Arizona which allowed strong to severe thunderstorms to form.
episodes.172512: A pre-frontal trough out ahead of a cold front was able to spark severe thunderstorms over an unstable environment in northeast NJ.
episodes.172514: A pre-frontal trough out ahead of a cold front was able to spark severe thunderstorms over an unstable environment in southeast NY.
episodes.172528: A pair of thunderstorms brought severe weather over northeastern South Dakota during the evening hours of July 20th. The storms produced quarter-size hail and 60 to 66 mph winds. Several trees and power lines were downed in Sisseton. A tree branch, about an inch in diameter, went through a shed roof in Sisseton.
episodes.172549: Monsoonal moisture created showers and thunderstorms over the higher terrain in northeast New Mexico and southeastern Colorado. These storms moved into the northwest combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles where the dry conditions at the surface helped created gusty conditions from rain cooled air. Thunderstorms generated severe wind gusts across the western Oklahoma Panhandle.
episodes.172550: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the central to eastern combined OK/TX Panhandles during the early evening of the 21st.  There was a severe wind gust reported in Armstrong County within the thunderstorm activity across the region.
episodes.172560: Thunderstorms tracked southeast during the overnight hours, with a few producing damaging wind gusts that blew down trees.
episodes.172682: During the afternoon and evening, scattered thunderstorms moved southwest off the Mogollon Rim into Cochise County where one storm produced hail that damaged drops near Pearce.
episodes.172731: A hot and humid airmass was in place across the northeastern United States ahead of an approaching cold front with these ingredients resulting in numerous showers and thunderstorms across New Hampshire and western Maine.  A long tracked severe thunderstorm with a history of producing large hail and damaging winds moved from central New Hampshire eastward into western Maine and caused significant damage, including concentrated wind damage in Moultonbourgh and Effingham, NH.
episodes.172732: A hot and humid airmass was in place across the northeastern United States ahead of an approaching cold front with these ingredients resulting in numerous showers and thunderstorms across New Hampshire and western Maine.  A severe thunderstorm|with a history of producing large hail and damaging winds moved from central New Hampshire eastward into western Maine and caused significant damage, including concentrated wind damage along the western shore of Sebago Lake due to a microburst. The storm was also accompanied by ping pong ball sized hail.
episodes.172762: A long track supercell thunderstorm developed ahead of a cold front pushing through the area on July 21st, 2022. The thunderstorms developed in an area with PWAT values up to 2.1 inches. The thunderstorm produced a quick 1 to 1.5 inches of rain in an hour.
episodes.172787: A humid airmass remained in place beneath a west-northwesterly flow aloft. Weak boundaries triggered convection in WNW to ESE oriented bands, some which were anchored to higher terrain. The result was excessive rainfall with training cells.
episodes.172791: A thunderstorm anchored and redeveloping over higher terrain near Marble NC produced up to 8 inches of rain.
episodes.172845: Wind and hail damage was reported across portions of Sargent County during the evening hours as an isolated severe thunderstorm impacted the area.
episodes.172879: A hot and humid airmass was in place across the northeastern United States ahead of an approaching cold front with these ingredients resulting in numerous showers and thunderstorms across New Hampshire and western Maine.  A severe thunderstorm|with a history of producing large hail and damaging winds moved from central New Hampshire eastward into the Seacoast and York County.  This storm moved off the coast bringing gusty winds to the nearshore waters.
episodes.172883: A pre-frontal trough out ahead of a cold front was able to spark severe thunderstorms over an unstable environment in southern CT.
episodes.172885: A pre-frontal trough out ahead of a cold front was able to spark severe thunderstorms over an unstable environment over the waters.
episodes.172987: A large cluster of severe thunderstorms moved southeastward out of Kentucky across northeastern Middle Tennessee during the early morning hours of July 21. Numerous reports of wind damage were received.
episodes.173069: Multiple waves of typical daytime summertime showers and thunderstorms developed within a modestly unstable and abnormally moist tropical airmass during the afternoon and evenings of July 19th through July 21st.  These storms produced numerous reports of trees and powerlines down, quarter size hail, and flash flooding across portions of north and central Georgia.

Training thunderstorms across the southern portion of the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar in San Miguel County produced an estimated 2 to 4 inches of rainfall within the Tecolote Creek and Gallinas Creek areas which caused significant and catastropic flash flooding. Flash flooding and debris flow washed out many roadways within the area, rendering them impassable. The camp director at the Camp Blue Haven said that their playground was underwater for about 40 minutes until water receded. At 2:40 PM MDT, the chief of the Cabo Lucero Volunteer Fire Department received a call about a vehicle floating within the flood waters. When officials responded to the floating vehicle, they also discovered two people dead nearby. While initially thought to have been in their vehicle, officials later determined that the two women, 62-year-old Linda June Cummings and 84-year-old Betty Greenhaw, were swept away from a destroyed home within the Tecolote Canyon subdivision. A third individual from the same home was reported missing, and the National Guard, New Mexico State Police, and San Miguel County Sheriff's Office assised in search and rescue for several days. Finally on Tuesday, July 26th, they found the body of 62-year-old Jimmy Chris Cummings. All three were from Hale Center, Texas, but had a 100-year-lease on a cabin in Tecolote Canyon on the Camp Blue Haven property which they were visiting at the time. Eight feet of water rushing down into the canyon took down two walls of the cabin and partially destroyed the other two walls. Damages for this event are estimated.

A long tracked severe thunderstorm and associated microburst reached the Moultonbourgh Neck area of Lake Winnipesaukee just after 3pm. The damaging winds downed over 200 trees on the western shore of the lake, with uprooted and snapped trees. The outflow winds then fanned across Moultonbourgh Bay, damaging trees on remote islands and the eastern shore of the lake where another area of concentrated damage occurred along the immediate shoreline.  Another 50 or so trees fell in this |area.  Overall 5 buildings were damaged but no injuries were reported. The storm continued to move eastward with continued sporadic damage though Ossipee before it reached Effingham, NH.

A microburst, with winds estimated at 90 mph began in Erving, MA and moved across Warwick, MA.  In Erving, the damage began along Route 2, which was closed for a time due to downed trees.  Trees, wires, and a power pole were down on Route 2 at East Prospect Street.  Trees and wires were down on a car on Camp Road. Numerous trees were downed on North Shore Road near Laurel Lake.

A NWS Survey concluded that a microburst, with winds estimated at 90 mph, began in Erving, MA and then moved across Warwick.  In Warwick, trees were down on Quarry Road and people were temporarily stranded at a campground just east of Quarry Road due to fallen trees.  By far, the most extensive damage occurred on Wendell Road east of the campground and on Hockanum Road in the Hockanum Hill section of Warwick.  There were more than a hundred trees downed, mainly pines.  Many were snapped mid-way up and others were uprooted.  Local Fire Department officials indicated that a couple of homes were hit by fallen trees on Wendell Road, one of which suffered damage to the property.  Trees fell in the same direction, from southwest to northeast, indicative of straight-line winds. There were many downed power lines.  Amazingly, no injuries were reported.

The long tracked severe thunderstorm that impacted the Moultonbourgh area strengthened once again as it traveled over Effingham, NH just after 3:30 PM. Widespread straight line wind damage began in western Effingham with a continuous area of wind damage concentrated along Town House Rd. Approximately 300 to 400 trees were either snapped or uprooted along this path of damage with sporadic tree damage throughout the town on other side roads.  Due to the observed almost |continues horizontal length of tree damage being near 4 miles, this outflow wind damage is characterized as a macroburst. A few buildings were damaged due to trees falling on roofs, but no injuries were reported from this event.
